_comment: Factory orchestrator policy (spine AD-7). backend: interactive (default, native Workflow launch) | claude-headless (native CLI) | opencode (integrated server dispatcher, independent build leases) | dry (read-only scheduler suggestions). autoApply stays false: humans author commits (KI-E1).
_buildCapacity: OpenCode backend maps this to dispatcher buildConcurrency: filesystem leases cover Node mechanics and worker commands using build-lease.mjs. Native interactive/claude-headless backends report advisory only. Arbitrary shell commands are not intercepted.
_includeEscalate: ESCALATED items need human judgment before re-dispatch — auto-running them risks wasted full-pipeline runs with 0 closures. Re-enable only for a specific targeted dispatch with --include-escalate flag.

autoCommit._comment: Server-mode only. Set enabled:true on a dedicated server to auto-commit CLOSED worktrees after each fold. Relaxes KI-E1 ('the human authors every commit') intentionally.

_escalationWebhook: Set to a Slack-compatible webhook URL to receive a POST when new items hit ESCALATED state. null disables.

autoFix._comment: Auto-reset FAILED items whose last-failure.json indicates a classifiable build/test error (csharp-compile, typescript-compile, msbuild-error, build-failed, test-failure, dotnet-error). maxRetries caps the per-item reset count to prevent infinite retry loops. Infrastructure failures (infraSuspect:true) are left to the driver's own infra-retry path. Set enabled:false to disable.

hillClimb._comment: KI-E278: hill-climbing run quality optimizer. Tracks close rate (fitness = closed/dispatched) per run. When fitness stagnates below plateauMinFitness for plateauRunsToTrigger consecutive runs, activates exploration mode: the next run deliberately selects items with the oldest lastScheduledCycle (items not tried recently), escaping local-maximum scheduling ruts. After one exploration run the mode resets. explorationRatio controls what fraction of the lane capacity is filled with exploration picks (vs the scheduler's default). See state/hill-climb.json for live state.

bandit._comment: KI-E279: UCB1 multi-armed bandit item selection. Each item is scored by closedRate + C*sqrt(ln(totalDispatches+1)/(dispatched+1)) where C=explorationConstant. Provides principled exploration/exploitation balance. Defers to hillClimb when exploration mode is active (hillClimb plateau-escape takes priority). State in state/bandit.json.

retrospective._comment: Periodic health report generator. Every runsPerRetro lanes, generates a markdown health report in queue/retrospective-<timestamp>.md with ledger state counts, close rate, and hill-climb fitness window. State in state/retrospective.json.

curriculum._comment: Curriculum learning. For never-tried (cold-start) items, replaces the uniform UCB1 exploration bonus with a difficulty-aware one: C*(1-estimatedDifficulty). Easier items get more exploration budget so the factory tries simple wins first. Difficulty is estimated from title word count, file count, and hard keyword matches. No extra state file — operates through bandit.json.

simulatedAnnealing._comment: Simulated annealing. Temperature T decays as T=T0*coolingRate^runCount. Each lane, with probability T, one selected item is swapped for a random READY item not in the selection — injecting controlled exploration that fades as the factory matures. State in state/simulated-annealing.json.

promptEvolution._comment: Prompt evolution. A/B tests two promptTemplate variants; after runsToEvaluate combined runs, kills the lower-close-rate variant and mutates the winner with a guidance phrase from a built-in library. Continuously evolves the worker prompt toward higher close rates. State in state/prompt-evolution.json.

itemTiming._comment: Dynamic timeouts. Records wall-clock elapsed milliseconds for each completed lane (last 100 samples). Computes P95+20% as recommendedTimeoutMinutes surfaced in the retrospective report, helping operators tune laneTimeoutMinutes. State in state/item-timing.json.

configOptimizer._comment: Config meta-optimizer. Every runsPerCycle lanes, perturbs one knob (rotating through bandit.explorationConstant, hillClimb.plateauMinFitness, hillClimb.explorationRatio, simulatedAnnealing.coolingRate) by +-perturbFraction, bounded to each knob's own sane range. Measures fitness over the next measureWindow runs vs the prior window and keeps or reverts. Modifies the live cfg in-memory only — never writes back to orchestrator.config.json. State in state/config-optimizer.json.

recalibrate._comment: Auto-recalibrate when stuck in a deep rut. When runsBelow consecutive runs all produce fitness < fitnessThreshold (deeper than hillClimb plateau), resets SA temperature to T0, boosts bandit exploration 1.5x for recoveryRuns lanes, and resets config-optimizer phase for a clean baseline. Manual: node orchestrate.mjs recalibrate. State in state/recalibrate.json.

claudeHeadless._extraArgs: KI-E277: the claude-headless backend runs fully unattended (no human at the terminal to answer a tool-approval prompt) — without this flag the worker would stall forever on the first prompt. Safety rests on the Workflow script's own constraints (no mutating git, worktree-scoped file access, agents only — KI-E1/KI-E2), not on interactive approval. Only applies to the claude-headless backend; the default interactive backend is unaffected.
claudeHeadless.promptTemplate: Operate as the AI-factory worker plane. Launch the Workflow tool on the script at {runScript} with NO args, wait for it to complete, then reply DONE. Do not run any git commands. Do not edit any file outside the per-item worktrees the script names.

confidenceThresholds._comment: Calibration gating thresholds (Kadavath et al. 2022). A probe whose confidence falls below its threshold is treated as uncertain and its negative verdict is skipped rather than triggering a costly plan revision or hard abort. Values here are the canonical reference; factory.js hardcodes the same defaults inline.

_weeklyTokenLimit: Estimated weekly output-token budget, used by logBatchTokenUsage() to show week-to-date consumption as a percentage so the operator can see which batches eat the weekly limit. 0 disables the percentage display. Set this to YOUR account's actual weekly limit to enable it — there is no universal default.
